+            # (heap invariant: every pair in stats has an entry with a count
+            # >= its current count; increases are pushed right away, decreases
+            # are re-filed here when their stale entry surfaces)
+            while heap:
+                c, pair = heap[0]
+                cur = stats_get(pair)
+                if cur == -c:
+                    break
+                heappop(heap)
+                if cur is not None and cur < -c:
+                    heappush(heap, (-cur, pair)) # count went down: re-file

+            top = -c
+            heappop(heap)
+            tied = None
+            while heap and heap[0][0] == c:
+                q = heappop(heap)[1]
+                cur = stats_get(q)
+                if cur == top:
+                    if tied is None:
+                        tied = {pair}
+                    tied.add(q)
+                elif cur is not None and cur < top:

actions.reason: The best change cut train_ir by only 0.71% (ratio 0.9929), short of the 1.0% minimum. It made RegexTokenizer.train push only increased pair counts onto the heap and re-file decreased ones lazily. Equivalence held and guard was ok. A second tweak, moving BasicTokenizer's tie-break scan into C with filter, changed nothing measurable. Most of what remains is probably interpreter startup and regex import, and finding more gain would need profiling I don't have budget for.
